name: SiFive HiFive1 Rev B
sources: SiFive FE310-G002 Manual v1p5 (memory map, CLINT, UART, PWM)
SiFive E31 Core Complex Manual (RV32IMAC, M and U modes, CLINT interrupt mode)
RISC-V Unprivileged ISA 20240411; RISC-V Privileged Architecture 20240411
QEMU 8.2.2 hw/riscv/sifive_e.c (machine sifive_e,revb=true) for independent execution

isa.notes: Every encoding outside RV32IMAC + Zicsr + Zifencei + MRET/WFI decodes to an illegal-instruction trap, as on the E31.

csrs.mstatus: MIE, MPIE, MPP only; a write that sets any other field is unsupported
csrs.mie: MSIE, MTIE, MEIE (other bits read as zero)
csrs.mtvec: direct (mode 0) and vectored (mode 1); other modes unsupported
csrs.mcause: read-only in the model (written by interrupt entry); a write is unsupported
csrs.mip: read returns environmental pending bits; writes have no effect
csrs.mhartid: reads 0; a write is an illegal-instruction trap

privilege.u_mode: MRET with MPP = U is unsupported (the scope never leaves M-mode)

boot.entry: ELF e_entry; the HiFive1 Rev B bootloader jumps to 0x20010000 in M-mode
assumptions: The hart is in M-mode at the entry point with mstatus.MIE = 0.
mstatus fields other than MIE, MPIE and MPP are zero (in particular MPRV = 0).
No PMP entry is locked, so PMP does not restrict M-mode accesses.
The flash holds exactly the image's PT_LOAD file bytes at their physical addresses and is not modified while the firmware runs.
Only the one hart runs, and no debugger, DMA master or other bus master accesses memory or devices.
arbitrary: mie (within its implemented bits), mtvec, mscratch, mepc, mcause

memory.name: dtim
memory.notes: Executable on hardware; fetching from it is unsupported in the model.

memory.name: flash
memory.notes: The 4 MiB SPI flash after the 64 KiB bootloader (the XIP window aliases beyond it; those addresses are not modeled). Only bytes the ELF places here are modeled; any other address is unsupported. Fetch requires an executable segment.

device_semantics: Reads of a listed register return an arbitrary word chosen by the environment, so any read side effect (such as popping the UART receive FIFO) cannot change what the proof covers. An accepted write is an observable event and has no other effect on the hart. Only aligned word accesses are modeled. An access to any unlisted address, including PRCI, AON, QSPI0, OTP, PLIC, GPIO, SPI, I2C, UART1 and PWM1/2, is unsupported: those devices can reset the chip, remap flash or change the clock.

interrupts.model: At every instruction boundary where mstatus.MIE = 1 and the cause's mie bit is set, the interrupt may be taken, whether or not the device would have it pending. This includes every behavior of the real timer, software and external sources and their priority order.
interrupts.nesting: Entry clears mstatus.MIE; MRET restores it from MPIE.

atomics: Single hart: an AMO is one indivisible read-modify-write in RAM. SC may succeed only while a reservation is held, and may always fail. AMO/LR/SC outside RAM is unsupported.
excluded: debug mode, NMIs, resets and watchdog expiry
bus errors on modeled addresses; ECC; power events
U-mode, PMP restrictions, the PLIC, DMA (the FE310 has none) and other bus masters
timing: cycle counts, interrupt latency, real-time deadlines
the bootloader, the flash programmer and the QSPI controller
